Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
Comments: International Internet bandwidth per Internet user reported as 1.99 kb/s in 2014.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Source (ITU data reproduced via TheGlobalEconomy.com) fetched and verified: international internet bandwidth per internet user was 1.99 kbit/s in 2014, the only figure available for Sierra Leone on this indicator. Additional searches (ITU DataHub, TeleGeography, Sierra Leone National Broadband Strategy 2023-2028) did not surface a more recent per-user bandwidth estimate. The cited figure correctly maps to the Very Low (<5 kbit/s) band, so the score stands, though the evidence is over a decade old and likely understates current capacity given subsequent submarine cable and fibre expansion.
revised_comments: International internet bandwidth per internet user in Sierra Leone stood at 1.99 kbit/s in 2014, according to ITU data, placing the country in the very low band (under 5 kbit/s per user). This remains the most recent internationally reported estimate available for this indicator.

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
Comments: Urban electricity access 54.69% vs rural 4.77% in 2020; gap = 49.92 percentage points (41–60pp band).
revision_notes: The original code of 1 (Gap >60pp) did not match the metadata scale even against its own cited 2020 figures (49.92pp falls in the 41-60pp band, i.e. code 2), indicating a scoring error. Verified directly on World Bank Open Data (SDG7.1.1 Electrification Dataset, ESMAP Tracking SDG7, dataset published 2023): urban electricity access was 56.3% and rural access 19.0% in 2023, a gap of 37.3 percentage points, which falls in the 21-40pp band (code 3). Rural access rose from around 5% in 2022 to 19% in 2023 in the same World Bank series; this is a large single-year jump, but comparable step-changes occur elsewhere in this series (e.g. 2016-2017) reflecting infrequent household-survey updates rather than data error. Given the size of the jump, flagging for human review to confirm before the higher code is accepted.
revised_comments: Access to electricity stood at 56.3% of the urban population against 19.0% of the rural population in 2023, according to World Bank Open Data (SDG7.1.1 Electrification Dataset), a gap of 37.3 percentage points. Rural electrification has improved from a very low base but remains substantially behind urban areas.
